Den Collective Photobooth

A tiny, cozy corner of the internet where every snap becomes a keepsake.

Slip behind the curtain, strike a pose, and watch your photo strip print itself, right in your browser. Pick a layout, dress it up with stickers, frames and hand-drawn flair, then save it, share it or print it.

How it works

Four easy steps from the curtain to your keepsake.

  1. 1

    Choose a layout

    Pick a photo strip, a grid or a Student ID card, or build your very own custom size.

  2. 2

    Strike a pose

    Allow the camera, get ready and let the countdown roll. Wave a hand to start, and redo any shot you are not happy with.

  3. 3

    Customize

    Dress your strip up with backgrounds, frames, stickers, templates and hand-drawn flair.

  4. 4

    Download

    Save it, turn it into a live GIF, share it with a QR code, or print it. It is all yours.

Far from your friend? Share one booth anyway.

  1. 1

    Open a booth

    Tap Join a Booth, then Create. Your own shared booth opens in seconds.

  2. 2

    Send the code

    You get a short booth ID. Tap Copy Invite, send it to your friend, and they tap Join and type it in.

  3. 3

    See each other live

    Video, voice and chat go straight between you. Your layout and timer stay in sync, and a tap splits the screen in half.

  4. 4

    Snap together

    Start the countdown and both booths shoot at the same time. Redo shots and dress up the strip together.

Got questions?

FAQ

Do I need to install an app?

No. Den Collective Photobooth runs right in your browser on your phone, tablet or computer. You can also add it to your home screen so it opens like an app.

Where do my photos go?

Your photos are made in your browser. They stay on your device unless you choose to share them, print them or use your account features.

Can I retake a photo I do not like?

Yes. Tap any photo to see it bigger, then press Redo to retake just that shot.

Can I use photos from my gallery instead of the camera?

Yes. On the camera screen, tap the small Gallery (picture) button beside Capture and choose your pictures. Drag and zoom each one to fit its spot, then tap Use photo.

Can I print my strip?

Yes. Open the menu, choose Print Setup, and set the paper and size for your printer.

How do I keep my account and templates safe?

Open the menu and choose Back up my account. Keep the file you download somewhere safe, and use it to restore your account if you ever lose it.

What is Den+?

Den+ is an optional upgrade that unlocks extra goodies, like custom themes. The photo booth itself works without it.

Printing

Print Setup

Connection
Setup guide: AirPrint / wireless
  1. Put the printer and your phone, tablet or laptop on the same Wi-Fi (not a guest network). A wired printer works too if it is connected to a wireless print server on that Wi-Fi.
  2. Use a printer that lists AirPrint (iPhone / iPad / Mac) or Mopria (Android) in its specs.
  3. Finish a session and tap Print, choose copies, then pick the printer in the system print window.
  4. In that window set the paper to the size shown in Den, scale 100% / Actual size, margins None, then Print.
  5. Run Test print below once to check alignment.
Setup guide: direct USB (no PC or laptop)
  1. Android phone / tablet: connect the printer with a USB cable and an OTG adapter (USB-C or micro-USB to USB-A/B, whichever your printer needs).
  2. Install the printer maker’s print plugin from Google Play once (or Mopria Print Service). Turn it on in Settings > Connected devices > Printing.
  3. Tap Print in Den: the USB printer appears in the print window. Pick it, check the paper size, Print.
  4. iPhone / iPad cannot print over USB directly. Use Option A, or plug the printer into a small wireless print server and use AirPrint.
  5. Keep the cable firmly in and the tablet charging during long events.
Printers

Example: strips on the main printer, 4×6 postcards on the secondary. The printer names are labels shown at print time; your device’s print window chooses the real printer.

Exposure

How-to connect Canon/Nikon/Sony camera?

A website can only receive the camera's video feed (like a webcam). It cannot trigger the shutter or download files from a DSLR, so we use the live feed. Your camera must show up as a webcam in the Camera list above.

Option A: USB straight to the camera (webcam mode)

  1. Charge the camera (or use a dummy battery / AC adapter) and set the lens to autofocus, or focus manually.
  2. Turn the camera on and set it to Movie / Video mode. Turn auto power-off and the screen timeout off.
  3. Plug a data-capable USB cable (not a charge-only cable) from the camera to your computer, tablet or phone.
  4. Sony: Menu > USB Connection > set USB Streaming (or PC Remote / webcam mode on older bodies, with the free Imaging Edge Webcam app).
  5. Canon: install EOS Webcam Utility on Windows/macOS, or on newer bodies choose the Video / webcam (UVC) USB mode.
  6. Nikon: install Nikon Webcam Utility, or on supported Z bodies set USB mode to the webcam (UVC) option.
  7. Open this menu > Camera Settings, tap Detect cameras, pick the camera, then Test camera.

Option B: HDMI + capture card (works with almost any DSLR/mirrorless)

  1. Set the camera's HDMI output to clean (no on-screen info) in its menu.
  2. Connect a mini/micro-HDMI to HDMI cable from the camera to a USB capture card (UVC type, e.g. Elgato Cam Link, or a generic USB 3.0 HDMI capture dongle).
  3. Plug the capture card into your device with its USB cable. Wait a few seconds, tap Detect cameras and choose the capture card (it appears as "USB Video", "Cam Link", "HDMI Capture", etc.).

Adapters for phones, tablets and laptops

  • Android phone/tablet: USB-C (or micro-USB) OTG adapter plus the camera's USB cable. The phone must support UVC cameras; Chrome lists them as a camera.
  • iPad / iPhone with USB-C: a direct USB-C cable or a USB-C hub works with UVC cameras and capture cards in recent iPadOS/iOS versions.
  • iPhone/iPad with Lightning: use Apple's Lightning to USB 3 Camera Adapter (with power connected) and a UVC capture card. Support varies by iOS version.
  • Laptops with USB-C only: use a USB-C to USB-A adapter or hub. Plug the camera directly into the laptop when possible, as hubs can limit video speed.
  • Keep cables short (under 3 m). For longer runs use an active, powered USB extension.

Using a second phone as the camera (USB cable)

  1. Android as the camera: plug it into the host with a data USB cable (USB-C to USB-C, or USB-C to USB-A plus an adapter). Open Settings > USB > Webcam (Android 14+ phones with webcam mode), or install a wired webcam app such as DroidCam or Iriun and enable USB debugging as the app asks. Then tap Detect cameras and pick it.
  2. iPhone as the camera: on a Mac use Continuity Camera (same Apple ID, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on, or a Lightning/USB-C cable). On Windows use a wired webcam app (e.g. Iriun or EpocCam) with the Lightning or USB-C cable and tap Trust This Computer.
  3. Mount the phone in landscape or portrait to match your layout, turn on Do Not Disturb, keep it on a charger, and stop the phone from sleeping while the booth runs.
  4. If the host is also a phone or tablet, use an OTG adapter (USB-C or Lightning Camera Adapter) between the two devices; support depends on the OS version.

Webcams

  1. Plug in the USB webcam (use an OTG adapter on phones/tablets), allow camera access, tap Detect cameras and select it.

Not showing up?

  • Try another cable (many are charge-only), another USB port, and close other apps using the camera (Zoom, OBS, the camera's own app).
  • Make sure the camera is in video/webcam mode and awake, then tap Detect cameras again.
  • Allow camera permission for this site in your browser settings. Use Chrome, Edge or Safari over https.
  • Manual exposure and white balance only work if the camera or driver exposes them to the browser. If the sliders are greyed out, set exposure and white balance on the camera body instead.

Privacy Policy

Effective Date: November 5, 2026

Welcome to Den Collective Photobooth ("we," "our," or "us"). We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting your personal data. This privacy policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you visit our website denphotobooth.online.

1. Information We Collect

We may collect information about you in a variety of ways, including:

  • Personal Data: When you sign in using Google or other authentication providers, we collect basic profile details such as your name, email address, and profile picture solely for authentication and session management.
  • Photobooth Data: Photos, custom templates, and session configurations you create or interact with while using our platform, which may be synced across your devices.
  • Usage Data: Information about how you access and use the website, including your browser type, device details, and interaction logs.

2. How We Use Your Information

Having accurate information permits us to provide you with a smooth, efficient, and customized experience. Specifically, we use information collected to:

  • Create and manage your user account and authenticate your identity securely.
  • Enable cloud synchronization of your photobooth sessions and preferences across multiple devices.
  • Improve website performance, features, and user experience.
  • Respond to customer service requests and support inquiries.

3. Disclosure of Your Information

We do not sell, trade, or otherwise transfer your personally identifiable information to outside parties, except to provide our services (such as secure hosting providers and authentication services like Google) or when required by law.

4. Security of Your Information

We use administrative, technical, and physical security measures designed to help protect your personal information from unauthorized access, disclosure, alteration, or destruction.

5. Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our practices or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons. We encourage you to review this page periodically.

6. Contact Us

If you have questions or comments about this Privacy Policy, please contact us through our website at denphotobooth.online.
